fixes: P1 (sync, hand-off timing): f1983 is built on live menu frame 30, but the overlay's engine-ready signal (#status opacity '0' -> finish() in intro_overlay_snippet.html) fires at about menu frame 1. praise: The frame delivers exactly what S26 and keyframe 6 ask for, and I checked the claims myself rather than taking them from the report. Outside the card, f1983 matches the live mf030 capture with max 0/255 and 0 px changed in both buckets. In 16:9 the only changed pixels sit inside the parchment field, bbox 266,357 to 1187,1343. Outside the card, the mean difference is 1.59/255 against the mf003 capture, 1.11/255 against mf120, and 0.001/255 against the second boot, all under G12. The shot content is all there: the no-save 5-button state, the game board with the camera still on its first focus (Grandbois), walnut beam, gold 'Chronica' valance, both lion banners, both candles at sprite art, carved lions, and in 4:3 the table edge the storyboard reserves for iPad aspects. Act V's 'no grade on the plate from f1798' holds by construction. At 100 % crops of all four corners and both side midpoints, the rebuilt blank parchment cannot be told from the game's own nine-patch: the inner dark line, the brass corners and the foxing are all continuous. The emotional read is immediate. The busy menu goes quiet, and one large empty page sits under the title in its walnut frame, so 'the chronicle waits for the player's hand' lands at a glance and sets up the card writing itself during the dissolve. Choosing menu frame 30 is the right call for the story, since it is the settled state S25 already promises by f1798. The corrected card size (629x665) is a real catch that protects the S24 f1766 leaf landing; I confirmed it independently on the original 1080p reference.
